title: just-deliver environment descriptor
description: What an environment publishes to the workloads deployed on it. name, region and type are addressable as env.name, env.region and env.type (the only env.* paths); a deployed part's export is read as ${<part>.<export>} from values. Checked against the catalog, not here: the type is declared, and a type with `approval: true` carries the `approval` block.

name.description: Environment name; same pattern as workload ids.

type.description: An environment type the catalog declares.

offers.description: The components and runtime the environment offers, as its definition names them; a shared layer's descriptor offers nothing, so no workload can deploy on it.

approval.description: The gate: an environment with this block accepts deploys only through `jd promote`. A set is promoted when it is qualified on `qualifiedOn` and `required` distinct listed approvers approved it. Literals, not expressions. Rules the schema cannot express: `qualifiedOn` is not this environment and `required` is at most the number of approvers.

qualifiedOn.description: The environment whose records must show the set qualified.

approvers.description: Entra object ids (lower case) that may approve.

separateFromDeployer.description: An approver may not be a principal that deployed the label on `qualifiedOn`. Required: a default would be a silent weakening.

values.description: The exports of the parts `jd env up` deployed, keyed by part name (values.<part>.<export>), the base descriptor's included: nested mappings of strings. Keys must not contain dots, so a dot path is unambiguous (enforced by the loader; the schema validator ignores propertyNames).
